Subject: Re: OmniHealth - Dedicated capacity commitment and validation plan

Jared —

Short answers: yes to VPC peering and KMS/HSM integration (we'll include the network checklist in the SOW). Regarding bursts, we recommend reserving burst pool capacity equivalent to 30% of committed GPUs for the first 90 days; this avoids throttling while the cache warms.

Sizing summary (from gpu-sizing-spreadsheet.csv):
- Primary cluster: 8 x A100-80GB (fp16) mapped to redwood/gpt-large expected to sustain 120 qps steady state at p95 latency ~180ms.
- Fallback cluster: 2 x A40-48GB (int8) for cost optimization during non-peak, used for batched embedding jobs and reranks.
- KV cache nodes: 2 x r5.4xlarge for prefix caching and session management.

Validation plan (high level):
1) Provision dedicated cluster and VPC peering (days 1–3)
2) Smoke test with sample traffic and model loading (day 4)
3) Two soak tests at 50% and 100% committed traffic (days 5–8)
4) Final cutover rehearsal and gradual traffic shift (days 9–10)

We will supply a runbook for the soak tests and a small load harness to simulate the burst profile. If Procurement needs a PO before DocuSign, we can accept PO with Net30 (Grace: FYI on billing ops).

—Ben
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: OmniHealth - validation runbook and cutover matrix

Folks —

Adding the proposed validation gates and a simple cutover/rollback matrix to ensure the staging window is actionable. Key items:

- Gate A (Provisioning): All nodes up, model versions pinned, network path validated (tests: ssh, DNS, KMS handshake). Pass -> Stage tests.
- Gate B (Functional & Latency): Run 250-case correctness suite; p95 latency under 220ms for 95% of requests; no crashes. Pass -> Soak.
- Gate C (Soak): 48-hour soak at 100% committed traffic with scheduled burst at hour 32. Monitor token cost, KV cache hit rate (>70%), and queue depth.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 300ms for >30 mins, error rate above 2%, or failed KMS operations.

Cutover week (proposed):
- Day -10 to -7: Provision and initial smoke
- Day -6 to -3: Full functional & latency tests (two runs)
- Day -2: Final soak run start (48 hours)
- Day 0: Gradual traffic shift (10% -> 50% -> 100% across 8 hours) with manual stop/go.

Hannah — please confirm billing start date alignment with the cutover day; we need to ensure Reserved capacity billing matches contract terms.

Thanks,
Karthik
Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
